outcome: A September 2025 preprint by Han, Liu, and Zhuang proves that general-type minimal model programs (MMPs) terminate — i.e. no infinite sequence of flips exists — in dimensions 4 and 5, with the fivefold big-boundary case and the effective (explicit step-bound) fourfold case both previously open; the general (non-general-type) termination question and dimension >5 remain open.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks whether infinite sequences of flips are possible in dimension >3 — i.e. whether termination of the MMP (Kawamata's termination-of-flips conjecture) is known beyond the threefold case, where Mori/Shokurov settled it. Prior to the window, termination in dimension 4 was known unconditionally (Fujino/Kawamata-era results and Birkar's later work; the frozen-date state of the art already had dimension-4 termination for arbitrary flips, per Fujino 2004/2005-era results, and separately Kawamata's termination for terminal fourfold flips). The 2025 preprint arXiv:2509.01501 (Han, Liu, Zhuang, 'Effective termination of general type MMPs in dimension at most five', submitted 2025-09-01, replacing an earlier two-paper split of arXiv:2506.20183) proves effective (explicitly bounded) termination of general type MMPs in dimension ≤5, and states plainly that termination of fivefold MMPs when K+Δ or Δ is big was not previously known, and that even the fourfold case with an explicit step bound was new. I read the paper's introduction directly (via fetch of the arXiv abstract and PDF) and found no mention of AI, machine learning, automated theorem proving, or formalization anywhere in the text — the proof is a purely human argument using Birkar's induction technique together with a new uniform bound on the Cartier index of Weil divisors in a general-type MMP, then invoking termination of terminal fourfold flips. This is scope-restricted to 'general type' pairs (K+Δ big, or pseudo-effective with Δ big), so it is a case of the stated problem rather than a full resolution — it does not touch non-general-type MMPs in dimension ≥4, nor any dimension above 5. Because it is a single preprint less than a year old with no evidence of expert digestion, journal acceptance, or a subsequent verification I could find, I classify it as 'partial' (a case of the problem is settled) rather than 'resolved' or 'claimed'; had the paper's status been merely an unverified announcement I would have used 'claimed', but a written, technically detailed preprint with named authors and a concrete argument is treated here as the evidentiary basis for the 'partial' case-settled classification, while noting the lack of digestion in confidence/summary. resolution_direction is 'confirmed' because the settled case (dimensions 4-5, general type) confirms termination as conjectured (no counterexample; flips do terminate in this case).
competing_reading: One could argue this preprint should be logged as merely 'progress' rather than 'partial', since it is scoped to general-type pairs and gives an *effective* (bounded) version of a result whose non-effective avatar in dimension 4 was arguably already implicit in earlier work (Fujino's termination of flips for fourfold MMPs, and Birkar's 2007 work using boundedness of pairs). If the paper's dimension-4 contribution is read as 'only' adding explicit bounds to an already-known qualitative termination result, then dimension 4 is not new territory and only the dimension-5 general-type case is a genuinely new settled case — still 'partial' under the same code, but with a narrower scope than stated above. This does not change the status code, only the extent of what was newly settled, which is reflected in outcome/summary.
what_would_settle_it: An explicit statement in a survey or in Han-Liu-Zhuang's related papers pinning down exactly which fourfold termination facts (qualitative vs. effective/bounded) were already established before this preprint, and whether any journal referee report or expert blog commentary (e.g. a birational-geometry seminar write-up) has appeared digesting arXiv:2509.01501.

events.what: Han, Liu and Zhuang prove (effective) termination of general type MMPs in dimension at most five, including the previously open fivefold case with K+Δ or Δ big

judgement.doubts: The record agrees with the derived codes. The bullet asks about all dimensions >3 and all flip sequences; the preprint covers only general-type MMPs in dimensions 4-5, so it is a case, and it is unreviewed, which does not affect a partial tier. The record says the preprint replaces an earlier split including arXiv:2506.20183 (June 2025), so the first written argument may predate 2025-09-01; either date is after the snapshot, so the status is unaffected. The record says the dimension-4 qualitative general-type case may already have been known before this paper; if so, the newly settled case is narrower (mainly dimension 5), but it is still a case. The Pith Review page was not opened and would not count as digestion anyway (F11).
